title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 158
paragraphs: So spoke the envoys; and Gelon came down on them very sharply, saying: “Greeks, it is a selfish speech with which you have dared to come and invite me to be your ally against the barbarian. When, some time ago, I asked you to join me in fighting an army of barbarians, a quarrel having arisen between me and the Carthaginians, and when I called upon you to take vengeance on the people of Egesta for the death of Dorieus son of Anaxandridas, while at the same time I offered to help you in freeing the trading posts, from which you have reaped great advantages and profits — then neither for my sake did you come to my aid, nor did you come to exact vengeance for the death of Dorieus. And as far as you are concerned, all those places are even now under the rule of barbarians. But since things turned out well for us and took a better course, now that the war has come round and reached you, at last a memory of Gelon has arisen in your minds. Even so, though I have been slighted by you, I will not act as you did; I am prepared to come to your aid, supplying two hundred triremes, twenty thousand hoplites, two thousand cavalry, two thousand archers, two thousand slingers, and two thousand light-armed men to run alongside the cavalry; and moreover I undertake to supply grain for the whole Greek army until we have finished the war. I pledge these things on this condition: that I be commander and leader of the Greeks against the barbarian. On any other terms I will neither come myself nor send others.”
